::: {#exm-lbfgs-step}
#### L-BFGS applies the update without forming the matrix

<!-- no-figure: the example compares two numerically equal vectors, and a plot of identical points shows nothing the printed table does not -->

Continue @exm-bfgs-step with $m = 1$ stored pair $(\vecf{s}^{(0)}, \vy^{(0)})$ and starting [matrix](linear-algebra-matrices.qmd#def-matrix) $\matr{I}_2$.
Below, $\matr{H}^+ \deriv{\vx} f(\vx^{(1)})$ is formed from vectors alone, starting from `H0`, then compared with the [matrix product](linear-algebra.qmd#def-matrix-mult).

```{r}
#| label: lbfgs-step
#| code-fold: false
g1 <- grad1
alpha <- rho * sum(s * g1)
q <- g1 - alpha * y
r <- drop(H0 %*% q)
beta <- rho * sum(y * r)
r <- r + s * (alpha - beta)
h1_g1 <- H1 %*% g1
from_matrix <- drop(h1_g1)
tibble::tibble(from_vectors = r, from_matrix = from_matrix)
```

The two columns agree to within `{r} format(max(abs(r - from_matrix)), digits = 2)`,
although the first never forms the matrix.
BFGS stores a dense $p \times p$ matrix and spends about $p^2$ operations per iteration;
L-BFGS stores $2m$ vectors with $p$ entries and spends about $m p$ operations per iteration, so it remains usable when $p$ is in the millions.

:::
